title: The day
description: Say when it is, and when things happen.
grammarNote: Tell the time with es la una, es la dos: es la una y media, es las tres.

explanation.summary: Telling the time in Spanish has one irregularity that catches everybody: after la una you do not say las, and after every other hour you do.

sections.heading: La una and las demás
sections.body: Es la una is one o'clock. Everything else is es las: es las dos, es las cinco, es las once. After la una you say la una y media, but after any other hour you say las tres y media. The same rule applies to the quarter: las cuatro y cuarto, but la una y cuarto.

sections.heading: A time of day is feminine
sections.body: La mañana, la tarde and la noche are all feminine, so you say por la mañana, por la tarde, por la noche. A day of the week is masculine instead, which is the opposite of English: el lunes, el martes. Do not mix them up.

examples.en: On Monday I have a meeting.

sections.heading: Saying when something happens
sections.body: A specific time goes with a, not con: a las tres, a las nueve de la noche. To say something happens every day, use todos los días or cada día. And for a time range, de a: de nueve a cinco.

examples.es: La reunión es a las tres.

examples.en: I work from nine to five.

items.note: Feminine: la hora. It also means the time.
In the phrase por la tarde. On its own it also means late.
In the phrase por la noche. It also means the night itself.
Masculine: el reloj. It also means a watch.

drills.note: After la una you do not say las.
After any other hour it is las and y media.
A time of day is feminine.
